body.en: A sequence is just an ordered list of numbers generated by a rule; a series is what you get when you add the terms of a sequence together. AIST Math 2 tests two specific families — arithmetic (constant difference) and geometric (constant ratio) — and one genuinely infinite idea: a sum with infinitely many terms that still adds up to a finite number.
body.ar: A المتتالية is just an ordered list of numbers generated by a rule; a المتسلسلة is what you get عندما you add the terms of a المتتالية together. AIST Math 2 tests two specific families — arithmetic (الثابت difference) and geometric (الثابت ratio) — and one genuinely infinite idea: a sum with infinitely many terms that still adds up to a finite number.

body.en:
A sequence \( a_1,a_2,a_3,\dots \) is arithmetic if consecutive terms differ by a constant \( d \), the common difference: \( a_{n+1}=a_n+d \). Its explicit (closed-form) formula is

\[ a_n=a_1+(n-1)d. \]
body.ar:
A المتتالية \( a_1,a_2,a_3,\dots \) is arithmetic if consecutive terms differ by a الثابت \( d \), the common difference: \( a_{n+1}=a_n+d \). Its explicit (closed-form) الصيغة is

\[ a_n=a_1+(n-1)d. \]

body.en:
An arithmetic series is the sum of an arithmetic sequence's first \( n \) terms. Pairing the first term with the last, the second with the second-to-last, and so on (each pair sums to \( a_1+a_n \)) gives

\[ S_n=\frac{n}{2}\big(a_1+a_n\big)=\frac{n}{2}\big(2a_1+(n-1)d\big). \]
body.ar:
An arithmetic series is the sum of an arithmetic المتتالية's first \( n \) terms. Pairing the first term with the last, the second with the second-to-last, and so on (each pair sums to \( a_1+a_n \)) gives

\[ S_n=\frac{n}{2}\big(a_1+a_n\big)=\frac{n}{2}\big(2a_1+(n-1)d\big). \]

\[ S_{10}=\frac{10}{2}\big(2(5)+9(3)\big)=5(10+27)=5(37)=185. \]

body.en:
A sequence is geometric if consecutive terms share a constant ratio \( r\neq0 \): \( a_{n+1}=r\,a_n \). Its explicit formula is

\[ a_n=a_1\,r^{\,n-1}. \]
body.ar:
A المتتالية is geometric if consecutive terms share a الثابت ratio \( r\neq0 \): \( a_{n+1}=r\,a_n \). Its explicit الصيغة is

\[ a_n=a_1\,r^{\,n-1}. \]

body.en:
A geometric sequence has \( a_1=3 \) and \( r=2 \). Find \( a_7 \).

\[ a_7=3\cdot2^{6}=3\cdot64=192. \]
body.ar:
A geometric المتتالية has \( a_1=3 \) and \( r=2 \). Find \( a_7 \).

\[ a_7=3\cdot2^{6}=3\cdot64=192. \]

body.en:
For \( r\neq1 \), the sum of the first \( n \) terms of a geometric sequence is

\[ S_n=\frac{a_1(r^n-1)}{r-1}. \]
body.ar:
For \( r\neq1 \), the sum of the first \( n \) terms of a geometric المتتالية is

\[ S_n=\frac{a_1(r^n-1)}{r-1}. \]

body.en: Write out \( S_n=a_1+a_1r+a_1r^2+\cdot s+a_1r^{n-1} \). Multiply both sides by \( r \): \[ rS_n=a_1r+a_1r^2+\cdot s+a_1r^{n-1}+a_1r^{n}. \] Subtract the first equation from the second — every middle term cancels (this is why the trick works), leaving \[ rS_n-S_n=a_1r^{n}-a_1. \] Factor: \( S_n(r-1)=a_1(r^n-1) \), and since \( r\neq1 \) we can divide by \( r-1 \) to get \( S_n=\dfrac{a_1(r^n-1)}{r-1} \). \( \blacksquare \)
body.ar: Write out \( S_n=a_1+a_1r+a_1r^2+\cdot s+a_1r^{n-1} \). Multiply both sides by \( r \): \[ rS_n=a_1r+a_1r^2+\cdot s+a_1r^{n-1}+a_1r^{n}. \] Subtract the first المعادلة from the second — every middle term cancels (this is why the trick works), leaving \[ rS_n-S_n=a_1r^{n}-a_1. \] Factor: \( S_n(r-1)=a_1(r^n-1) \), and since \( r\neq1 \) we can divide by \( r-1 \) to get \( S_n=\dfrac{a_1(r^n-1)}{r-1} \). \( \blacksquare \)

label.en: Worked example 3.D — Sum a geometric series
label.ar: مثال محلول 3.D — Sum a geometric المتسلسلة

body.en:
If \( |r|<1 \), the infinite geometric series \( a_1+a_1r+a_1r^2+\cdot s \) converges to

\[ S_\infty=\frac{a_1}{1-r}. \] If \( |r|\geq1 \) (and \( a_1\neq0 \)), the series diverges — it has no finite sum.
body.ar:
If \( |r|<1 \), the infinite geometric المتسلسلة \( a_1+a_1r+a_1r^2+\cdot s \) converges to

\[ S_\infty=\frac{a_1}{1-r}. \] If \( |r|\geq1 \) (and \( a_1\neq0 \)), the المتسلسلة diverges — it has no finite sum.

body.en: By Theorem 3.1, \( S_n=\dfrac{a_1(r^n-1)}{r-1}=\dfrac{a_1}{1-r}\big(1-r^n\big) \) (multiplying numerator and denominator by \( -1 \)). When \( |r|<1 \), repeated multiplication by a number smaller than \( 1 \) in absolute value shrinks \( r^n\to0 \) as \( n\to\infty \) (e.g. \( r=\tfrac12 \) gives \( \tfrac12,\tfrac14,\tfrac18,\dots\to0 \)). So \( S_n\to\dfrac{a_1}{1-r}(1-0)=\dfrac{a_1}{1-r} \), which is exactly \( S_\infty \). When \( |r|\geq1 \), \( r^n \) does not shrink to \( 0 \) (it stays constant at \( |a_1| \) or grows without bound), so \( S_n \) never settles on a finite value. \( \blacksquare \)
body.ar: By مبرهنة 3.1, \( S_n=\dfrac{a_1(r^n-1)}{r-1}=\dfrac{a_1}{1-r}\big(1-r^n\big) \) (multiplying numerator and denominator by \( -1 \)). عندما \( |r|<1 \), repeated multiplication by a number smaller than \( 1 \) in absolute value shrinks \( r^n\to0 \) as \( n\to\infty \) (e.g. \( r=\tfrac12 \) gives \( \tfrac12,\tfrac14,\tfrac18,\dots\to0 \)). So \( S_n\to\dfrac{a_1}{1-r}(1-0)=\dfrac{a_1}{1-r} \), which is exactly \( S_\infty \). عندما \( |r|\geq1 \), \( r^n \) does not shrink to \( 0 \) (it stays الثابت at \( |a_1| \) or grows without bound), so \( S_n \) never settles on a finite value. \( \blacksquare \)

body.en:
Find \( 8+4+2+1+\cdot s \).

Here \( a_1=8 \) and \( r=\tfrac12 \) (each term is half the last), and \( |r|=\tfrac12<1 \), so Theorem 3.2 applies: \[ S_\infty=\frac{8}{1-\tfrac12}=\frac{8}{\tfrac12}=16. \]

body.en:
Convergence Restriction: The infinite geometric sum formula \(S_\infty = \dfrac{a_1}{1-r}\) is only valid when \(|r| < 1\). If \(|r| \geq 1\), the series diverges and has no finite sum.

Term Index Off-by-One: Remember the exponent is \(n-1\), not \(n\): \(a_n = a_1 r^{n-1}\) and \(a_n = a_1 + (n-1)d\). A common error is writing \(a_5 = a_1 r^5\) instead of \(a_1 r^4\).

Arithmetic Term Count: When using \(S_n = \dfrac{n}{2}(a_1 + a_n)\), ensure \(n\) is determined correctly via \(n = \dfrac{a_n - a_1}{d} + 1\).

question.en: The second term of a geometric sequence is \( 12 \) and the fifth term is \( \dfrac{32}{9} \). Find the common ratio \( r \), the first term \( a_1 \), and the sum of the infinite series \( S_\infty \).
question.ar: The second term of a geometric sequence is \( 12 \) and the fإذا كانth term is \( \dfrac{32}{9} \). أوجد common ratio \( r \), the first term \( a_1 \), and the sum of the infinite series \( S_\infty \).

solution.en:
Step 1: Express terms in terms of \( a_1 \) and \( r \):
\[ a_2 = a_1 r = 12 \] \[ a_5 = a_1 r^4 = \frac{32}{9} \]

Step 2: Divide \( a_5 \) by \( a_2 \):
\[ \frac{a_1 r^4}{a_1 r} = r^3 = \frac{32/9}{12} = \frac{32}{108} = \frac{8}{27} \]

Step 3: Extract the common ratio \( r \):
\[ r = \sqrt[3]{\frac{8}{27}} = \mathbf{\frac{2}{3}}. \]

Step 4: Find \( a_1 \):
\[ a_1\left(\frac{2}{3}\right) = 12 \implies a_1 = 12 \times \frac{3}{2} = \mathbf{18}. \]

Step 5: Compute the infinite sum \( S_\infty \):
Since \( |r| = \frac{2}{3} < 1 \), Theorem 3.2 guarantees convergence:
\[ S_\infty = \frac{a_1}{1 - r} = \frac{18}{1 - 2/3} = \frac{18}{1/3} = \mathbf{54}. \]

question.en: In an arithmetic sequence, the 4th term is \( 17 \) and the 10th term is \( 41 \). Determine the common difference \( d \), the first term \( a_1 \), and the partial sum of terms from \( a_{11} \) through \( a_{25} \) inclusive.
question.ar: In an arithmetic sequence, the 4th term is \( 17 \) and the 10th term is \( 41 \). حدّد common dإذا كانference \( d \), the first term \( a_1 \), and the partial sum of terms from \( a_{11} \) through \( a_{25} \) inclusive.

solution.en:
Step 1: Solve for common difference \( d \):
\[ a_{10} - a_4 = (10 - 4)d = 6d \] \[ 41 - 17 = 24 \implies 6d = 24 \implies \mathbf{d = 4}. \]

Step 2: Solve for the first term \( a_1 \):
\[ a_4 = a_1 + 3d \implies 17 = a_1 + 3(4) \implies a_1 = 17 - 12 = \mathbf{5}. \]

Step 3: Find boundary terms for the range \( n = 11 \) to \( 25 \):
Number of terms: \( N = 25 - 11 + 1 = 15 \).
Term \( a_{11} = a_1 + 10d = 5 + 10(4) = 45 \).
Term \( a_{25} = a_1 + 24d = 5 + 24(4) = 5 + 96 = 101 \).

Step 4: Compute the sum:
\[ \sum_{k=11}^{25} a_k = \frac{N}{2}\big(a_{11} + a_{25}\big) = \frac{15}{2}(45 + 101) = \frac{15}{2}(146) = 15 \times 73 = \mathbf{1095}. \]

question.en: Express the repeating decimal \( 0.3\overline{18} = 0.3181818\dots \) as an irreducible fraction using the infinite geometric series formula.
question.ar: Express the repeating decimal \( 0.3\overline{18} = 0.3181818\dots \) as an irreducible fraction باستخدام infinite geometric series formula.

solution.en:
Step 1: Separate the non-repeating and repeating components:
\[ 0.3\overline{18} = \frac{3}{10} + 0.0181818\dots \]

Step 2: Represent the repeating part as an infinite geometric series:
\[ 0.0181818\dots = \frac{18}{1000} + \frac{18}{100000} + \cdot s \]
Here the initial term is \( a_1 = \frac{18}{1000} \) and the common ratio is \( r = \frac{1}{100} \).

Step 3: Sum the geometric series:
\[ S_\infty = \frac{a_1}{1 - r} = \frac{\frac{18}{1000}}{1 - \frac{1}{100}} = \frac{\frac{18}{1000}}{\frac{99}{100}} = \frac{18}{1000} \times \frac{100}{99} = \frac{18}{990} = \frac{2}{110} = \frac{1}{55}. \]

Step 4: Combine with the initial non-repeating term:
\[ 0.3\overline{18} = \frac{3}{10} + \frac{1}{55} = \frac{33}{110} + \frac{2}{110} = \frac{35}{110} = \mathbf{\frac{7}{22}}. \]
(Verification: \( 7 \div 22 = 0.3181818\dots \) ✓).

question.en: Evaluate the exact value of the telescoping sum: \[ \sum_{k=1}^{50} \left( \frac{1}{k} - \frac{1}{k+1} \right) \] and evaluate the convergent infinite series: \[ \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{3}{4^n}. \]
question.ar: احسب قيمة the exact value of the telescoping sum: \[ \sum_{k=1}^{50} \left( \frac{1}{k} - \frac{1}{k+1} \right) \] and احسب قيمة the convergent infinite series: \[ \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{3}{4^n}. \]

solution.en:
Part 1: Telescoping sum:
Write out the first few and last terms:
\[ \left(1 - \frac{1}{2}\right) + \left(\frac{1}{2} - \frac{1}{3}\right) + \cdot s + \left(\frac{1}{50} - \frac{1}{51}\right) \]
All intermediate terms cancel pairwise, leaving:
\[ 1 - \frac{1}{51} = \mathbf{\frac{50}{51}}. \]

Part 2: Infinite series:
Factor the numerator and identify initial term and ratio:
\[ \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{3}{4^n} = \frac{3}{4} + \frac{3}{16} + \frac{3}{64} + \cdot s \]
Initial term \( a_1 = \frac{3}{4} \), ratio \( r = \frac{1}{4} \).
\[ S_\infty = \frac{a_1}{1 - r} = \frac{3/4}{1 - 1/4} = \frac{3/4}{3/4} = \mathbf{1}. \]

question.en: The first four terms of an arithmetic sequence are 5, 12, 19, and 26. What is the 20th term of this sequence?
question.ar: حل المسألة التالية في (Sequences & Series): The first four terms of an arithmetic sequence are 5, 12, 19, and 26. What is the 20th term of this sequence?

hints.en: To find the 20th term of the arithmetic sequence, first identify the initial term and the common difference: 1. The first term is \( a_1 = 5 \).
hints.ar: To أوجد 20th term of the arithmetic sequence, first identإذا كانy the initial term and the common dإذا كانference: 1. The first term is \( a_1 = 5 \).

hints.en: The common difference \( d \) is found by subtracting consecutive terms: \( d = 12 - 5 = 7 \). The general formula for the \( n \)th term of an arithmetic sequence is: \(a_n = a_1 + (n - 1)d\).
hints.ar: The common dإذا كانference \( d \) is found by subtracting consecutive terms: \( d = 12 - 5 = 7 \). The general formula for the \( n \)th term of an arithmetic sequence is: \(a_n = a_1 + (n - 1)d\).

solution.en:
To find the 20th term of the arithmetic sequence, first identify the initial term and the common difference:

1. The first term is \( a_1 = 5 \).
2. The common difference \( d \) is found by subtracting consecutive terms: \( d = 12 - 5 = 7 \).

The general formula for the \( n \)th term of an arithmetic sequence is:
\[ a_n = a_1 + (n - 1)d \]

Substitute \( n = 20 \), \( a_1 = 5 \), and \( d = 7 \):
\[ a_{20} = 5 + (20 - 1)(7) = 5 + 19(7) = 5 + 133 = 138 \]

Common misconceptions:
- Using \( n \) instead of \( n - 1 \) yields \( 5 + 20(7) = 145 \).
- Calculating \( 20 \times 7 = 140 \) overlooks the starting value \( a_1 = 5 \).
- Using \( n - 2 \) steps yields \( 5 + 18(7) = 131 \).
